claims.text: The Calphad method can be used to control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Calphad predicts phase equilibria in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Calphad predictions can guide alloy design.
Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys contain multiple constituent phases.
Constituent phases and their corresponding transformations mediate phase evolution.
Ab initio calculations can predict phase equilibria and guide alloy design.
Molecular dynamics simulations can predict phase equilibria and guide alloy design.
Traditional alloy-design methods result in uncontrolled phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Traditional alloy-design methods have limitations relevant to controlling phase evolution.
Understanding of phase transformations in high-entropy alloys is limited.
The accuracy of Calphad phase-equilibrium predictions for complex Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and intervention identify Calphad as the operative method, whereas the mechanism substitutes ab initio calculations or molecular dynamics. These are distinct computational approaches, and no relationship explaining how they constitute or support the proposed Calphad mechanism is provided.
